title: Dynamically Enabled Robustness of Geometric Phases and Entanglement in the Nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings Model
summary: Robustness in dissipative light-matter systems has recently been associated with resonance conditions or geodesic evolution. We show that, in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, these conditions are necessary but not sufficient. Using a Kerr-type extension together with a Lindblad description of cavity losses and atomic decoherence, we identify a dynamically enabled mechanism in which the stability of geometric phases and entanglement is governed by the alignment between coherent and dissipative trajectories in Hilbert space.
